subject: Re: ACME - feature parity & next tests (streaming, tool-calling, structured output)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME - follow-up: competitive eval & next tests

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can make your hyperscaler comparison as apples-to-apples as possible.

Recap / where Redwood shone in the demo:
- Streaming: consistent low tail latency with configurable time-to-first-token and partial-token streaming (we can stream structured JSON chunks).
- Function/tool calling: first-class support for deterministic function signatures (JSON Schema + type hints) and automatic structured outputs for downstream parsing.
- Cost/latency controls: intelligent batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization profiles we can suggest based on your sequence distribution.
- Reliability: fallback routing to compatible model variants and per-route SLOs — useful for production-critical paths you mentioned.

Competitive notes (high level):
- Hyperscalers (Vertex/Bedrock): strong on model catalog and integration with cloud infra; less opinionated on batching/caching for inference economics, and streaming semantics vary by provider.
- Redwood: focused on predictable inference economics + production features (rollouts, tracing, per-token breakdowns) that matter when you have high throughput and tight latency constraints.

Proposed next tests (what we suggest you run vs Vertex/Bedrock):
1) Streaming latency/throughput: run two 1-hour sessions at 50/200 RPS with your typical prompt mix; measure time-to-first-token, 95/99 latency, and end-to-end client experience.
2) Tool/function-calling: wire a function that returns structured JSON (payment authorization flow sample you mentioned). Validate schema adherence, retry semantics, and end-to-end callback wiring.
3) Structured outputs & parsing: test structured output extraction across noisy prompts (we'll supply a 150-case prompt set).
4) Fallback & quantization: simulate a burst where we fallback to a quantized variant to observe quality vs cost delta.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-20260914.pdf (short comparison), test-plan-acme-20260914.xlsx (proposed stimuli and metrics), demo-recording-20260913.mp4 (streaming demo excerpt).

Can you confirm success criteria for each test (latency targets, acceptance thresholds for structured outputs) and whether your team prefers hosted sandbox tests or a short-lived Private deployment in your VPC for the function-calling tests?

Proposed times for the kickoff test run: Wed 2026-09-16 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 2026-09-17 09:00-10:00 PT. Let me know which works and I'll loop in engineering.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme.com>

Subject: Re: ACME - follow-up: competitive eval & next tests

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few quick clarifications before we lock a slot: 

1) Function-calling: can you share example request/response payloads (schema) you'd use for an authorization flow? We want to make sure our internal orchestration matches.
2) Hosted vs VPC: for POC we prefer hosted sandbox if it preserves audit logs; for anything that hits customer PII we'll need a VPC/private run. Can Redwood run the function-call test inside our VPC for the second round?
3) Metrics: our bar for streaming is 200ms median TTF and 800ms p95 for short prompts — are those reasonable on your side?

Also, procurement has asked for an indicative pricing delta vs Bedrock for the same throughput profile — can you share a ballpark range? Not looking for a formal quote yet.

Regards,
Emily Zhang
Senior Product Manager, ACME Corp

Date: 2026-09-13T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - follow-up: competitive eval & next tests

Emily — great questions, answers inline and attached a short test-plan we can iterate on.

1) Example function-calling payloads: attached the JSON Schema + 5 example invocations in the spreadsheet (test-plan-acme-20260914.xlsx). Example (high level):

Request: {
  "function": "authorize_payment",
  "args": {"amount": 125.00, "currency": "USD", "card_last4": "4242", "merchant_id": "acme_store_1"}
}

Response (expected structured JSON): {
  "status": "approved",
  "auth_code": "ABCD1234",
  "confidence": 0.94,
  "raw_model_trace": "..."
}

We'll provide a strict schema and validation harness so you can grade pass/fail automatically.

2) Hosted vs VPC: for the initial round we recommend hosted sandbox (faster to stand up and gives you the streaming telemetry). For the function-calling test that touches PII we can run a one-week Private deployment in your VPC — engineering will provision a short-lived endpoint and keys. Marcus/Aditya — can you confirm ETA for a short-lived private endpoint?

3) Streaming targets: 200ms median TTF and 800ms p95 for short prompts are reasonable targets for our smaller model families; depending on prompt length and RPS we may need to suggest a different model configuration. We'll instrument to capture TTF, p50/p95/p99, and token throughput as part of the plan.

Pricing ballpark: for the throughput profile you mentioned (50-200 RPS), you should expect a 10-25% delta vs Bedrock depending on batching and caching. We'll provide a more tailored estimate after the first test run.

I've attached the redwood-vs-hyperscalers-20260914.pdf with a quick matrix and the test plan spreadsheet with stimuli. If that looks good I'll lock Wed 9/16 10am PT and get engineering on the invite.

Best,
Marissa
